reason: The gridded form of the resident field is delivered and measured. The fill draws on a regular lattice in the viewport's projection, so its raster is geographically placed, and the GPU-sampled value at a screen position matches the CPU reference at that position's geography to 4.17e-07, inside the unchanged 2e-5 bound. The missing rule and the global-grid wraparound match the CPU reference, the fill and the barbs stay independently updatable, and the payload fits the declared ceilings. The interaction contract is whole again: the gridded form's staging is now part of the field's own sampling pass, so a resident time window's members are prepared in the idle time the interactive pipeline leaves, and the native gate is green on every check (pan 0/120, zoom 0/24, time 0/18, continuous_weather true). The disagreement the first pass left open is settled: the framebuffer measurement was taken in the widget's logical pixels while the framebuffer is in device pixels, so it read a painted region two times too small and away from the hole; the fill's behaviour was never wrong. Measured in the framebuffer's own scale, the missing node's own cell contributes exactly zero alpha pixels and the hole it leaves is two lattice cells wide in each axis, and the gate now reads that measurement. The bound is not relaxed, the source selection is not changed, and the visual verdict stays deferred.

second_pass.status: complete: the native gate passed on the first of the three allowed attempts, and the missing-node disagreement is settled.

budget.first_pass_overrun_disclosed: The first pass ran eight native viewport-interaction attempts against a recorded budget of three. The overrun stays on the record in this file (gate.native_attempts = 8) and is not hidden or rewritten by this pass.

preparation_cost.method: One field preparation on the 22-source fixture, the same script for both revisions, a fresh sampler per run and the median of five runs. The 'sampling' rows are the deterministic warm measurements of the sampler's own passes over the field's 11506 native nodes and the lattice's 4002 nodes, in the same process, so they compare the two shapes directly.
what_changed: The lattice's nodes are sampled in the field's own pass, so the gridded form adds no second pass over the weather: the field's sampling with the gridded form fell from 135.4 ms to 44.2 ms (a 91 ms saving per field).

The grid-relative vector rotation needed the true east/north unit vector at every corner of every stencil, and a raster node is the corner of four neighbouring stencils, so the geodesic inverse was repeated four times for the same point. The basis is now computed once per distinct corner and gathered back; every value is unchanged and the field's own sampling fell from 99.7 ms to 35.1 ms.

The `grid` argument of stage_field was shadowed by the loop over the sources' grids, so the gridded form was staged whether or not it was asked for. The argument is honoured now, which is what the flag has always meant: the independent viewport stages the gridded form only when the numerical fill is enabled.
preparation_cost.comparison_basis: These rows measure the viewport's own field preparation on the fixture, not the recorded baselines of docs/profiles/rendering/2026-10-19/prepare-breakdown.json (792 ms cold, 159 ms for a re-centred window), which were taken on a different script: they include the per-node land loop's first-call cost and the first endpoint-image encoding, and they were measured before the sampling and land memos existed. The rows above are the same script before and after this pass, so the difference between the two revisions is the measurement; the difference between a row and the recorded baseline is not.
preparation_cost.fidelity: No value changed. The lattice's values are the CPU sampler's values at the lattice's node positions, bit for bit: the merged pass samples the same positions with the same sampler, and the corner basis is the same number per point as before.

missing_node.settled: The fill's behaviour was correct; the probe measured in the wrong coordinate space.
missing_node.cause: The probe counted the alpha of a neighbourhood around the missing node using the view's logical pixels, while the framebuffer it read is in device pixels (the fixture's display is 2x, so the framebuffer is 1800x1400 for a 900x700 widget). The neighbourhood was therefore read at half the size and half the offset of the hole, in a region the fill had painted: 529 painted pixels. The probe also used the camera the check was handed, not the camera the widget was showing after the independence observation had moved it by 0.01 degrees.
missing_node.corrected_measurement: Measured in the framebuffer's own scale and against the camera the widget is showing, the missing node's own cell (2025 device pixels, 45x45) contributes exactly 0 alpha pixels and 0 significant alpha pixels; the hole the missing node leaves is 7744 device pixels, a box of rows 652-739 and columns 816-903, which is 44x44 logical pixels: two lattice cells wide in each axis, because the shader's 2x2 bilinear reads the missing corner over two cells. The rest of the frame is painted: 2512256 of 2520000 pixels.
missing_node.gate: The viewport-interaction gate now reads the corrected measurement: the missing node's own cell must contribute exactly zero alpha pixels, and it does.
missing_node.unchanged: The byte-exact readback agreed with the shader all along: the cell that touches the missing node reads back as missing and a cell away from it is still painted. No behaviour changed to settle this.

lattice.decision: The resident field carries a second form: a regular lattice in the viewport's projection, so the shader's 2x2 texelFetch bilinear is a geographic interpolation instead of an interpolation over a packed node list.
lattice.space: The viewport's projection: longitude and the spherical Mercator ordinate, both in degrees. The projection is conformal, so one spacing serves both axes and a cell is a square on the ground.

spacing.derivation: The finest contributing wind source's own cell: its latitude axis, in metres (HRDPS 20261018 00z, 0.0225 degree of arc = 2505 m), measured in the viewport's projection at the window's centre latitude (48.31 N): 2505 m / (111319 m/degree * cos(48.31)) = 0.0338275 degrees. The spacing is derived from the sources' resolution and the window; no number is invented.

alternatives_measured.the source's resolution in degrees of ar: 8755 nodes, the same source cell, and the resident time window's members cost 0.20 s each; the gate's time-crossings phase showed 5 of 18 inputs loading
alternatives_measured.the source's cell in the projection (ado: 4002 nodes, 0.05 s of extra staging per field

origin.rule: The lattice's north-west cell corner is quantised outward on the global grid (a multiple of the spacing), so the lattice always covers the window and keeps its position when the window moves. The rows run from north to south, the order a texture's rows have.
origin.relation_to_the_window: The lattice covers the field's geographic window (47.6855 N - 124.2281 E to 48.9285 N - 121.9657 E), which is the resident field's window (the camera's 1.5x window, quantised on the 64 px field lattice).

lattice.values: The CPU sampler's values at the lattice's node positions (the sampler's own bilinear in the winning source's raster space), so the CPU sampler stays the reference authority and no weather is decoded a second time. A missing node stays missing.
lattice.cost: no extra decode; one extra sampling pass over the lattice's nodes, taken from the same worker

placement.method: The CPU mirror of the shader's arithmetic, as recorded by issue #68, applied to the gridded payload and anchored at the geographic position: the screen position is projected into the viewport's projection, the viewport's own rectangle for the lattice maps it to a texture position, and the GPU's value is read back through the #71 byte-exact readback of the application's weather shader.
placement.cpu_reference: The CPU's own interpolation of the same field at that position, the reference the recorded 2e-5 gate uses (tools/experiment_float_textures.py's bilinear_reference).

placement_error_before.form: the node-list form: the packed 64-column node list, which the shader interpolated linearly across the viewport
placement_error_before.note: The node list is not a raster: the value the shader painted at a screen position was the node list's interpolation at a texture position, not the field's value at that position's geography.

placement_error_after.note: The remaining difference is the lattice's resampling of the CPU sampler's own bilinear: the field is carried at the source's cell size, and the sampler's interpolation inside a cell is not linear. It is a property of the gridded form, not of the GPU's arithmetic: the GPU's arithmetic reproduces the CPU's interpolation of the same field to 4.17e-07.

missing.rule: A missing sample is never filled from a neighbour and never becomes the field minimum: the shader rejects a NaN or infinite corner and contributes exactly zero alpha (the A0k rule, unchanged).

missing_node.note: The gridded payload with one missing node: the cell that touches the node reads back as missing and contributes no alpha at all in the framebuffer, a cell away from it is still painted, and the hole is two lattice cells wide in each axis.

wraparound.rule: The global-grid wraparound matches the CPU reference: a longitude is taken into the lattice's own branch of the global grid, so a window across the antimeridian is not split between two cells, and a wrapped node carries the sampler's wrapped value.
wraparound.cell_continuity: the cell index at 179.999 is 11.5147 and at 180.001 is 11.5742: the seam is not a cell boundary and the two sides are the same cells.
wraparound.sampler_wrap: the CPU sampler's own values: sample_at(180.0) equals sample_at(-180.0) for both periodic GRIB files in the fixture (7.30468225479126 and 15.123397827148438), the ±360 wrap the lattice inherits.
wraparound.coverage: At the fixture's forecast instant no selected source covers the antimeridian, so the seam's values are missing there and the fill is transparent rather than interpolating across the gap.

payload.note: The gridded form's values and images are accounted with the field (16 bytes of float32 per node and 32 bytes of RGBA8888 texture per node). The retained payload is 20.7% of the 128 MiB ceiling with 13 fields and no eviction. The sampling memo holds 12.8 MB of its 16 MiB ceiling with no eviction.

The gridded form adds a second sampling pass (0.05 s) to every member's preparation, and the member the camera reaches at input 7 is the last the idle worker prepares. This is the revision the gate asks for; the source selection, the bound and the thresholds are unchanged.

the CPU sampler's role as the reference authority and the fallback path
the application's default path: the gridded form is staged only when the numerical fill is enabled (--gpu-weather-fill, default off)
endpoint: QQuickWindow.afterRendering render-callback proxy; the pixel readbacks are framebuffer readbacks (fidelity), not presentation FPS, not input-to-present and not scanout.
visual_fidelity: deferred and not evaluated. This artifact reports pixels, masks and values, not a visual verdict.
limits: The gridded form is a resampling: the field is carried at the source's cell size, so the fill's value at a position differs from the CPU sampler's own interpolation there by up to 0.126 m/s (mean 0.019 m/s) over the fixture's window. The GPU's arithmetic reproduces the CPU's interpolation of the same field to 4.17e-07. The resampling figure compares against the sampler's own value at the position's geography; it is not a gate threshold.

The lattice's spacing is derived at the window's centre latitude, so a window at another latitude gets a lattice at that latitude's scale; the lattice's origin is quantised on the global grid, so the fill's raster shifts by at most a cell when the window moves.

The fixture's resident field at the gate's camera is single-source (the HRDPS 20261018 00z run covers the whole window), so the gate's positions do not cover a source boundary; the sources' provenance was measured over the window (576 positions, all HRDPS) and at the antimeridian (no coverage at the fixture's instant).
The readbacks are fidelity measurements. No presentation latency, input-to-present time or frame rate is claimed.
The visual verdict stays deferred: this artifact reports pixels, masks and values, not a visual verdict.
next_step: The geographic portrayal of the fill is delivered and the interaction contract is whole. The next concrete step is the visual ratification of the fill's portrayal (the deferred visual verdict), not another change to the gridded form.
